title: the Marlowe Estate Rising Again
premise: When small-town coroner Marguerite Nystrom supervises the ceremonial exhumation of town founder Elias Marlowe, he finds the coffin empty—and a fresh body buried beneath it, killed within the last year. Following a coded ledger hidden in the estate's gravestone inscriptions, Marguerite uncovers a vigilante network of townspeople who have been quietly disappearing abusers and predators the law failed to convict. As the sheriff closes in on the network and someone begins silencing its members, Marguerite must decide whether justice outside the law deserves protection or exposure—ending with him burning the ledger's final page, adopting the found family of conspirators as his own, and filing the empty coffin away as the town's last shared secret.
about_author: C. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former rural records clerk who spent a decade alphabetizing other people's secrets in a county basement. Hartwell now writes mysteries about quiet people who know too much, from a farmhouse full of rescued animals.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Marguerite Nystrom's POV. Establishes his meticulous, invisible life as coroner of Hollow Creek, his ritual of knowing every grave by name, and his careful distance from the townsfolk who barely see him. The centennial committee orders Elias Marlowe's coffin exhumed for relocation to a memorial crypt. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as order.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The exhumation draws half the town; when the lid comes off, the founder's coffin holds only century-old air—and beneath it, a second, unmarked coffin holding a recent corpse: Dale Pruitt, a man everyone assumed had simply moved away. Emotional beat: shock cracking open Marguerite's carefully sealed world.

chapters.title: Filed Under P
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with a flashback interlude. He quietly investigates Pruitt's disappearance three years prior—a case the sheriff closed as a runaway. Digging through his own files, he finds Pruitt's death certificate was never filed, meaning someone with access to records made him vanish. Emotional beat: suspicion turning inward, toward people he knows.

chapters.title: Stones That Speak
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A retired schoolteacher, Odessa Vann, notices him studying the Marlowe Estate cemetery and shows him that certain gravestone dates don't match parish records—the discrepancies form a cipher pointing to a ledger hidden in the estate chapel's foundation. Emotional beat: first true connection; belonging offered cautiously.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Inside the chapel wall he finds a leather ledger begun by Elias Marlowe himself: names of wrongdoers the courts failed, paired with dates and small marks. The most recent entries are in living handwriting—including Pruitt's name, marked complete. Emotional beat: dread and terrible fascination.

chapters.title: The Quiet Congregation
chapters.summary: Odessa's POV. She reveals the truth: the network spans generations—nurse, mechanic, diner owner—people who bury what the law forgives. They've kept the ledger as both record and warning. Someone inside has started killing members instead of targets; two are already dead. Emotional beat: found family extended to Marguerite, at a price.

chapters.title: What the Sheriff Knows
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Sheriff Dane Colter, outwardly investigating the empty coffin, privately reveals he's known about the network for years and looked away—but now bodies are piling up and pressure from the state is forcing his hand. He gives Marguerite seventy-two hours before arrests begin. Emotional beat: justice and law circling each other warily.

chapters.title: The Marked Page
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Cross-referencing handwriting and the cipher, Marguerite identifies the killer: the memorial committee chairman, Harlan Boyd, Marlowe's great-grandson, using the network's methods to erase witnesses to his own embezzlement and an old hit-and-run. But Boyd learns Marguerite has the ledger. Emotional beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: Night at the Estate
chapters.summary: Alternating Marguerite and Odessa POVs. Boyd lures Marguerite to the Marlowe Estate to burn the ledger with him inside; Odessa and the network intervene. In the chapel confrontation, Boyd confesses before the gathered town, and the sheriff arrives—not to save Marguerite, but to hear it all. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into witness.

chapters.title: A Name for Every Grave
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Boyd is convicted; the network dissolves itself, trusting the law it once bypassed because Marguerite testified that justice must be seen to belong to everyone. At the reburial, they lay Elias Marlowe's memory—and Pruitt—to rest properly, and Marguerite carves his own name into the town's ledger of the living. Emotional beat: belonging earned, invisibility willingly surrendered.
